panelIntro: Freeze a frame and the lab will show you which parts of the picture pushed the answer towards a class.
needFrame: Freeze a frame first, then ask for an explanation.
needModel: Train the model first. There is nothing to explain until it has learned something.
failed: The heat map could not be worked out. Your photos and your model are fine — try again.

framing.evidenceNotReason: This shows where the evidence was, not the reason for the answer. The model does not have reasons — it has patterns of pixels that pushed the score one way or the other.
framing.notProof: A heat map is a clue about the model, not proof that the model is right. Two different methods can point at different places, and neither is guaranteed correct.
framing.relativeScale: Colours are relative to this map only. The brightest spot in a weak explanation looks exactly like the brightest spot in a strong one, so you cannot compare brightness between two maps.
framing.coarse: The heat map is worked out on a {{size}}×{{size}} grid and then stretched over the photo, so it is blurry on purpose. It can tell you roughly where, not exactly what.

legend.caption: Where the evidence for this class was strongest.

classSelector.label: Explain which class
classSelector.hint: You can ask about any class, not only the one it chose. Asking why it did NOT pick the other class is often more interesting.

opacity.label: Heat map strength
opacity.hint: Slide it down to see the photo underneath.

detail.label: Finer detail
detail.hint: Uses an earlier layer, giving a 14×14 grid instead of 7×7. Finer is not automatically better — compare them and see.

alt.heading: In words
alt.concentrated: The strongest evidence for "{{name}}" is in the {{vertical}} {{horizontal}} of the picture.
alt.diffuse: The evidence for "{{name}}" is spread across much of the picture rather than concentrated anywhere, so the map is not really pointing at one thing.
alt.degenerate: No evidence could be worked out for "{{name}}" on this frame. That usually means the model barely distinguishes this class at all.
alt.coverage: About {{percent}}% of the picture carries at least half the strongest evidence.

cached: Shown from what was worked out a moment ago.
onDevice: The heat map was worked out on this device and is not uploaded anywhere.

compare.heading: Compare two explanations
compare.intro: Two completely different methods, on the same frozen frame, for the same class. Where they agree you can be a bit more confident. Where they disagree, that is worth knowing too.
compare.gradcamHow: Asks the model which parts of the picture, if nudged, would change its score the most. Fast, but it works on a coarse grid.
compare.occlusionHow: Covers one square at a time and measures how much the score drops. Slower, but it makes no assumptions about how the model works — it just asks it {{count}} times.

agreement.heading: Do they agree?
agreement.overlap: They pick the same hottest areas {{percent}}% of the time.
agreement.strong: These two methods mostly agree. Two different ways of asking gave a similar answer, which is a reason to take it a bit more seriously.
agreement.partial: These two methods partly agree. They overlap, but each is also looking somewhere the other is not.
agreement.disagreementWarning: When two methods disagree, NEITHER of them is guaranteed to be right. The lab is not going to pick one for you or average them together — the disagreement is the finding. It usually means the model is relying on something fragile, and that is worth investigating rather than smoothing over.
agreement.noBlend: The two maps are shown separately, side by side, on purpose. Averaging them would hide exactly the thing you should be looking at.

compare.budget: Covering up takes a few seconds because it asks the model {{count}} separate questions. You can stop it at any time.
compare.coarseGrid: This device is running the slower fallback, or has a small screen, so the covering-up map uses a {{size}}×{{size}} grid instead of 12×12. Both explanations still run — the second one is just a little chunkier.
